issues.description: Twenty author-code inputs are identified. A bounded SAS metadata/readability probe confirms all eleven R05-consumed fields are present and readable in the common COMP.FUNDA candidate. This does not verify the author-native file, target population/history, units, identifier meaning, or producer construction; the other required input routes also retain their documented unknowns. The native route and full data compatibility remain unresolved, without implying absence or a license barrier.

The merger workflow reads subsidy_mergers_raw_for_thomson without a documented producer, imports a separate hand-checked match file, and references CIK fields differently across two consumers of the inherited subsidy workbook. Those producer, header, and coverage contracts are unresolved.

The assembler exports Data/cik_for_board_data_upload.txt while R reads Data/Board/cik_for_boardex_upload.csv. R writes the scraped output under Data/Board, while the Stata pcon builder reads Data/DEF14A_scraped_connected_firms.csv. These author-defined handoffs need path/name staging and import-format checks.

The R source comments out the governor assignment at line 55 and later reads a governor column at line 100. Before that parser, the assigned source QA records the stacked filing rows and a rowSums any-connection construction. Enabling the commented expression may change the connection construction; the current evidence does not establish a harmless repair or the intended column lineage.

Bounded Stata 18 checks found eststo, winsor, and coefplot but did not report their add-on versions, and did not find reclink in the checked command paths; bounded R metadata did not find the six named package distributions. Official dplyr documentation identifies bind_rows as a documented provider, while installed-release/API and paper-specific input-object compatibility remain untested. The remaining items are ordinary setup and version-preparation tasks; no software was installed, no package was loaded, and no author code was run.

The complete target spans merger preparation, subsidy generation, a two-pass assembler, an R/Stata board handoff, pcon generation, and analysis. Several inputs and producer/schema mappings remain unverified, so the full workflow dependency closure is not established.
